EXPLANATION: The strong band at 1231 cm⁻¹ fits a ν(C=S) thiocarbonyl stretch (consistent with bond-order placement per FRQ-001), and the very intense 648 cm⁻¹ peak lies in the C–Cl/C–S heavy-atom stretching region (supported by the C–Cl ranges in GFQ-046). The prominent 805 cm⁻¹ feature is compatible with halogen-related bending modes in chlorinated aliphatics. Aliphatic C–H stretches at 2854–2972 cm⁻¹ and CH deformation at 1437 cm⁻¹ match GFQ-003. Absence of a strong ~1030 cm⁻¹ ν(S=O) (sulfoxide) or ~1700 cm⁻¹ ν(C=O) (sultone) disfavors sulfoxide/sultone candidates, and the SO₂ doublet (~1300/1150) expected for sulfones is not evident. Overall, CC(Cl)C=S best explains the observed pattern.
